# AWS Explained Simply

> A free, independent educational reference that explains every Amazon Web Services
> product in plain English, with an honest note on when NOT to use each one. It also
> holds 51 reference architectures from a one page site up to global scale, a sandbox
> for sketching a setup and seeing a rough cost, and a catalogue of AWS certifications.

Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Amazon Web Services.
All prices quoted are rough teaching estimates, never quotes.
Written by Mihir Joshi. Distributed by 4Bit Technology.
Last updated 2026-09-30.

## Start here

- [Before AWS: the words nobody explained](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/): 31 fundamentals, from what a server is to what DNS does, explained with nothing assumed.
- [How AWS itself works](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/learn.html): why there are 300 services, the eight to learn first, and how the billing actually works.
- [What should I actually build](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/architecture.html): 51 architectures keyed to the reader's own situation, with cost, capacity ceiling, what breaks first and what not to build yet.
- [All services](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/services.html): the full index.
- [Playground](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/playground.html): sketch an architecture and see a rough monthly cost.
- [AWS certifications](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/certifications.html): every current exam with code, price, domains and status.

## Every service, explained


### AI and Machine Learning

- [AWS App Studio](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-app-studio.html): Describe a business app in plain words and it builds a working one for you.
- [AWS Deep Learning AMIs](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-deep-learning-amis.html): A ready-made server image with the AI tools already installed.
- [AWS Deep Learning Containers](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-deep-learning-containers.html): Prebuilt Docker images with PyTorch and its GPU parts already working.
- [AWS DeepRacer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-deepracer.html): A toy race car game that taught people reinforcement learning, now shut down as an AWS service.
- [AWS Elemental Inference](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-inference.html): A media focused machine learning capability. We could not confirm the current details.
- [AWS HealthImaging](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-healthimaging.html): Storage for hospital scan images that keeps them fast to open.
- [AWS HealthLake](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-healthlake.html): A place to put patient records so you can search and analyse them.
- [AWS HealthOmics](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-healthomics.html): Runs genetics analysis pipelines and stores the huge files they produce.
- [AWS HealthScribe](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-healthscribe.html): Listens to a doctor and patient talking and writes up the clinical note.
- [AWS Neuron](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-neuron.html): The free software kit that lets your model run on AWS's own AI chips.
- [AWS Panorama](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-panorama.html): A discontinued box that ran computer vision on existing security cameras.
- [Amazon Augmented AI A2I](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-augmented-ai-a2i.html): Sends the AI's unsure answers to a human to check.
- [Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-bedrock.html): Use ready made AI models, including Claude, through one API.
- [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-bedrock-agentcore.html): Runs an AI agent as a live service, with memory and tools attached.
- [Amazon CodeGuru](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-codeguru.html): Reviewed your code and found slow spots in running apps, and is now mostly closed.
- [Amazon CodeWhisperer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-codewhisperer.html): The old name for AWS code autocomplete, now folded into Amazon Q Developer.
- [Amazon Comprehend](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-comprehend.html): Finds meaning inside plain text.
- [Amazon Comprehend Medical](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-comprehend-medical.html): Pulls medicines, doses, conditions and symptoms out of doctors' notes.
- [Amazon DevOps Guru](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-devops-guru.html): Watches your AWS metrics and tells you when something looks wrong and probably why.
- [Amazon Elastic Inference](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elastic-inference.html): A retired way to bolt a slice of a GPU onto a normal server.
- [Amazon Forecast](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-forecast.html): Predicted future numbers from your past numbers, and is closed to new customers.
- [Amazon Fraud Detector](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-fraud-detector.html): Scores an online action as likely fraud or not, using your own past cases.
- [Amazon Kendra](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-kendra.html): A search box for your company's documents that understands questions, not just keywords.
- [Amazon Lex](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-lex.html): Builds a chatbot or phone bot that works out what the caller wants.
- [Amazon Lookout for Equipment](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-lookout-for-equipment.html): Learns the normal readings of a machine and warns when they drift, and it is being shut down.
- [Amazon Lookout for Vision](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-lookout-for-vision.html): Spotted defects in photos of products on a line, and has been discontinued.
- [Amazon Monitron](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-monitron.html): A sensor you stick on a motor that warns when it starts running badly, no longer sold to new customers.
- [Amazon Nova](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-nova.html): Amazon's own family of AI models, sold through Bedrock.
- [Amazon Personalize](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-personalize.html): Builds the "you might also like" list for your site from what your users actually did.
- [Amazon Polly](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-polly.html): Turns written text into a natural sounding voice.
- [Amazon Q](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-q.html): An AI assistant for AWS work, split into one for developers and one for business users.
- [Amazon Rekognition](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-rekognition.html): Understands what is in a picture or video.
- [Amazon SageMaker AI](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-sagemaker-ai.html): Build and train your own machine learning models.
- [Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-sagemaker-ground-truth.html): Gets humans to label your training data, and manages the whole labelling job.
- [Amazon SageMaker Studio Lab](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-sagemaker-studio-lab.html): A free notebook for learning machine learning, with no AWS account, now closing to new users.
- [Amazon Textract](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-textract.html): Pulls text and tables out of scanned documents.
- [Amazon Transcribe](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-transcribe.html): Turns speech into written text.
- [Amazon Translate](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-translate.html): Translates text between languages.
- [Apache MXNet on AWS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/apache-mxnet-on-aws.html): AWS support for an old deep learning framework that is no longer maintained.
- [PyTorch on AWS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/pytorch-on-aws.html): Not a service, just the many ways to run the PyTorch framework on AWS.
- [TensorFlow on AWS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/tensorflow-on-aws.html): Not a service. It is the ways you can run the TensorFlow library on AWS.

### Analytics

- [AWS Clean Rooms](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-clean-rooms.html): Two companies compare their customer data without either one handing the data over.
- [AWS Data Exchange](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-data-exchange.html): A shop inside AWS where you buy or sell data sets and keep them updated automatically.
- [AWS Entity Resolution](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-entity-resolution.html): Works out which records in different files are the same person or company.
- [AWS Glue](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-glue.html): Cleans and moves data between places.
- [AWS Glue DataBrew](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-glue-databrew.html): A point-and-click tool for cleaning up messy data without writing code.
- [AWS Lake Formation](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-lake-formation.html): Decides who is allowed to see which tables, columns and rows of your data in S3.
- [Amazon Athena](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-athena.html): Run SQL directly on files sitting in S3.
- [Amazon CloudSearch](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-cloudsearch.html): An old search box service for websites, now closed to new customers.
- [Amazon Data Firehose](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-data-firehose.html): Takes a constant trickle of records and drops them into storage for you, in batches.
- [Amazon DataZone](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-datazone.html): A catalogue where staff can find the company's data and ask for permission to use it.
- [Amazon EMR](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-emr.html): Big data processing with Spark and Hadoop.
- [Amazon FinSpace](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-finspace.html): A data store built for finance firms, now being shut down.
- [Amazon Kinesis](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-kinesis.html): Handles data that never stops arriving.
- [Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-kinesis-data-streams.html): A pipe that holds a stream of events for a while so several programs can read them.
- [Amazon Kinesis Video Streams](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-kinesis-video-streams.html): It takes video from cameras and stores it so software can watch it back or analyse it.
- [Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-managed-service-for-apache-flink.html): Runs code that does sums over a live stream of events, like a running total per minute.
- [Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-managed-streaming-for-apache-kafka.html): AWS runs Apache Kafka for you so you do not have to babysit the servers.
- [Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-opensearch-service.html): A search engine you can point at your logs or your website content.
- [Amazon Redshift](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-redshift.html): A warehouse built for asking big questions of big data.
- [Amazon SageMaker](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-sagemaker.html): The place to build, train and run your own machine learning models on AWS.

### Application Integration

- [AWS AppSync](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-appsync.html): A managed GraphQL API.
- [AWS B2B Data Interchange](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-b2b-data-interchange.html): It turns the old-fashioned trading files big companies exchange into JSON your software can read, and back again.
- [AWS Express Workflows](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-express-workflows.html): A fast, cheap mode of AWS Step Functions for very high volume, short jobs.
- [AWS Step Functions](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-step-functions.html): Draws your multi step process as a flowchart that actually runs.
- [Amazon AppFlow](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-appflow.html): A managed way to move data between business apps like Salesforce or SAP and AWS, without writing the plumbing.
- [Amazon EventBridge](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-eventbridge.html): A router for events between services.
- [Amazon MQ](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-mq.html): It runs ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ for you, so old applications keep talking the way they already do.
- [Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-managed-workflows-for-apache-airflow.html): It runs Apache Airflow for you, so scheduled data pipelines have somewhere to live.
- [Amazon Simple Notification Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-simple-notification-service.html): Sends one message to many listeners at once.
- [Amazon Simple Queue Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-simple-queue-service.html): A waiting line for tasks.

### Blockchain

- [Amazon Managed Blockchain](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-managed-blockchain.html): Runs blockchain networks so you do not have to operate the nodes yourself.

### Business Applications

- [AWS AppFabric](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-appfabric.html): It pulls the activity logs out of your SaaS apps and puts them in one place.
- [AWS End User Messaging](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-end-user-messaging.html): It sends SMS, voice calls and phone push notifications from your code.
- [AWS Supply Chain](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-supply-chain.html): It reads your existing ERP data and warns you when stock is about to run short.
- [AWS Wickr](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-wickr.html): An end-to-end encrypted chat and calling app for organisations that need messages to stay secret.
- [Amazon Chime](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-chime.html): Amazon's own video meetings app, which is being switched off.
- [Amazon Chime SDK](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-chime-sdk.html): Building blocks for putting video calls, audio and chat inside your own app.
- [Amazon Connect](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-connect.html): A ready-made call centre you set up in a browser instead of buying phone hardware.
- [Amazon Pinpoint](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-pinpoint.html): A marketing messaging service that AWS is closing down.
- [Amazon Pinpoint APIs](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-pinpoint-apis.html): The older set of Pinpoint APIs for customer messaging, most of which stop working in October 2026.
- [Amazon Quick](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-quick.html): The new umbrella name for Amazon QuickSight plus AI agents that answer questions about your business data.
- [Amazon Simple Email Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-simple-email-service.html): Sends email from your app, cheaply and at scale.
- [Amazon WorkDocs](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-workdocs.html): Amazon's file storage and sharing service for staff, now switched off.
- [Amazon WorkDocs SDK](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-workdocs-sdk.html): The programming interface to Amazon WorkDocs, a file sharing service AWS has closed to new customers.
- [Amazon WorkMail](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-workmail.html): AWS business email and calendar. It is being shut down on 31 March 2027.

### Compute

- [AWS App Runner](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-app-runner.html): Give it your code or container, it runs a web service.
- [AWS Batch](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-batch.html): Runs large numbers of background jobs.
- [AWS Compute Optimizer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-compute-optimizer.html): Looks at how hard your servers actually work and tells you which ones are too big.
- [AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elastic-beanstalk.html): Upload your code and AWS sets up the servers for you.
- [AWS Lambda](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-lambda.html): Run a small piece of code without owning a server.
- [AWS Local Zones](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-local-zones.html): Small AWS outposts in extra cities, so your servers sit closer to users there.
- [AWS Nitro Enclaves](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-nitro-enclaves.html): A sealed side room on your server where secret data can be processed and nobody, not even you, can look in.
- [AWS Outposts family](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-outposts-family.html): AWS ships actual racks or small boxes of its own hardware to your building and runs them for you.
- [AWS Outposts rack](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-outposts-rack.html): Puts a full rack of AWS hardware inside your own building.
- [AWS Outposts servers](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-outposts-servers.html): A single AWS server box you put in a shop, clinic or factory.
- [AWS Parallel Cluster](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-parallel-cluster.html): Sets up a cluster of machines that run scientific jobs in a queue.
- [AWS Parallel Computing Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-parallel-computing-service.html): It runs a proper scientific computing cluster for you, using the Slurm scheduler researchers already know.
- [AWS Serverless Application Repository](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-serverless-application-repository.html): A catalogue of ready-made small AWS apps you can deploy into your own account in a few clicks.
- [AWS SimSpace Weaver](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-simspace-weaver.html): A retired service that used to spread one huge simulated world across many servers.
- [AWS Wavelength](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-wavelength.html): AWS servers placed inside mobile phone networks, so phone apps reach them without crossing the wider internet.
- [Amazon DCV](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-dcv.html): Lets you use a graphics heavy desktop that is running somewhere else.
- [Amazon EC2](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-ec2.html): A computer you rent in Amazon's data centre.
- [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html): Adds servers when busy, removes them when quiet.
- [Amazon EC2 Image Builder](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-ec2-image-builder.html): It builds your standard server image for you, on a schedule, with your software and patches baked in.
- [Amazon Elastic VMware Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elastic-vmware-service.html): It runs VMware Cloud Foundation on AWS hardware, inside your own network.
- [Amazon Lightsail](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-lightsail.html): A simple server at a fixed monthly price.
- [Amazon Lightsail for Research](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-lightsail-for-research.html): A simple rented desktop in the cloud with research software like RStudio or JupyterLab already installed.
- [Bottlerocket](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/bottlerocket.html): A stripped down operating system for machines that only run containers.
- [Elastic Fabric Adapter](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/elastic-fabric-adapter.html): A special network card for EC2 that lets many servers talk to each other extremely fast.

### Containers

- [AWS Fargate](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-fargate.html): Runs containers without you owning any servers.
- [Amazon ECS Anywhere](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-ecs-anywhere.html): Lets AWS run and manage containers on servers you own, not AWS servers.
- [Amazon EKS Anywhere](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-eks-anywhere.html): Runs AWS style Kubernetes clusters on your own servers.
- [Amazon EKS Distro](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-eks-distro.html): The exact Kubernetes build AWS itself runs, handed to you as open source.
- [Amazon Elastic Container Registry](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elastic-container-registry.html): A private store for your container images.
- [Amazon Elastic Container Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elastic-container-service.html): Runs your app in containers, the simple AWS way.
- [Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elastic-kubernetes-service.html): Managed Kubernetes.
- [Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/red-hat-openshift-service-on-aws.html): Red Hat's OpenShift, run for you inside your AWS account.

### Cost and Billing

- [AWS Billing Conductor](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-billing-conductor.html): It lets you send someone a different AWS bill than the one AWS actually produced.
- [AWS Budgets](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-budgets.html): It emails you when your AWS spending passes a number you picked.
- [AWS Cost Explorer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cost-explorer.html): Shows where your AWS money is going.
- [AWS Cost and Usage Report](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cost-and-usage-report.html): It drops a giant spreadsheet of every line of your AWS bill into an S3 bucket.
- [AWS FinOps Agent](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-finops-agent.html): An AI agent that watches your AWS bill, investigates cost spikes and answers cost questions in plain English.
- [Reserved Instance Reporting](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/reserved-instance-reporting.html): It is the screen that tells you whether the capacity you pre-paid for is actually being used.
- [Savings Plans](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/savings-plans.html): A pricing commitment, not a service. You promise to spend a set amount per hour for one or three years and pay less per hour.

### Customer Enablement

- [AWS Activate](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-activate.html): Free AWS credits and help for new startups.
- [AWS IQ](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iq.html): A retired marketplace where you hired freelance AWS experts by the project.
- [AWS Managed Services](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-managed-services.html): You pay AWS staff to run your AWS infrastructure operations for you.
- [AWS Professional Services](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-professional-services.html): AWS consultants you pay to come and build or advise on a project with you.
- [AWS Support](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-support.html): A paid plan that lets you raise a ticket and get a human at AWS to help.
- [AWS Training Certification](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-training-certification.html): AWS courses and exams, some free, that prove you know the services.
- [AWS rePost](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-repost.html): A free public question and answer site for AWS, run by AWS.
- [AWS rePost Private](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-repost-private.html): A private version of the re:Post question site, just for your company. It is being shut down.

### Databases

- [AWS Database Migration Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-database-migration-service.html): Moves a database into AWS with almost no downtime.
- [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-aurora.html): Amazon's faster version of MySQL and PostgreSQL.
- [Amazon DocumentDB](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-documentdb.html): It is a database that speaks MongoDB's language but is built and run by AWS.
- [Amazon DynamoDB](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-dynamodb.html): A very fast database with no tables to join.
- [Amazon ElastiCache](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elasticache.html): Keeps frequently used data in memory so it is fast.
- [Amazon Keyspaces](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-keyspaces.html): It stores data the way Apache Cassandra does, without you running any Cassandra servers.
- [Amazon MemoryDB](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-memorydb.html): It is a very fast in-memory store that, unlike a normal cache, does not lose your data.
- [Amazon Neptune](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-neptune.html): It is a database for things that are connected to other things, and for the connections themselves.
- [Amazon RDS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-rds.html): A normal SQL database, run for you.
- [Amazon Timestream](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-timestream.html): It stores readings that arrive with a timestamp, like sensor or metric data.
- [Oracle Database at AWS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/oracle-database-at-aws.html): Runs real Oracle Exadata databases inside an AWS data centre, next to your apps.

### Developer Tools

- [AWS Cloud Control API](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloud-control-api.html): One set of five commands to create, read, update, delete and list almost any AWS thing.
- [AWS Cloud Development Kit](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloud-development-kit.html): Write your AWS setup as normal code instead of a long config file.
- [AWS Cloud9](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloud9.html): A code editor that ran in your browser, now closed to new customers.
- [AWS CloudShell](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloudshell.html): A terminal inside the AWS website that already knows who you are.
- [AWS CodeArtifact](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-codeartifact.html): A private store for the code libraries your team installs.
- [AWS CodeBuild](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-codebuild.html): A machine AWS starts for you to compile and test your code, then throws away.
- [AWS CodeCommit](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-codecommit.html): AWS's own private Git repository hosting.
- [AWS CodeDeploy](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-codedeploy.html): Puts a new version of your app onto servers gradually, and rolls back if it breaks.
- [AWS CodePipeline](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-codepipeline.html): Joins the steps from code change to live release into one automatic chain.
- [AWS Command Line Interface](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-command-line-interface.html): Type AWS commands in a terminal instead of clicking around the website.
- [AWS Fault Injection Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-fault-injection-service.html): Deliberately breaks parts of your system so you can see how it copes.
- [AWS Infrastructure Composer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-infrastructure-composer.html): Draw your AWS setup on a canvas and get the config file out of it.
- [AWS Tools and SDKs](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-tools-and-sdks.html): The official libraries that let your program talk to AWS.
- [AWS X Ray](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-x-ray.html): Follows one request through all your services and shows where the time went.
- [Amazon CodeCatalyst](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-codecatalyst.html): AWS's all in one place for repos, pipelines and issues, now in maintenance mode.
- [Amazon Corretto](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-corretto.html): Amazon's free version of Java, which they keep patched for years.

### End User Computing

- [Amazon WorkSpaces](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-workspaces.html): Gives each person a Windows or Linux desktop they open from any device.

### Front End Web and Mobile

- [AWS Amplify](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-amplify.html): The quickest way to put a web or mobile front end online.
- [AWS Device Farm](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-device-farm.html): Lets you test your app on real phones and tablets sitting in an AWS data centre.
- [Amazon Location Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-location-service.html): Maps, address lookup, routes and location tracking for your app, without a Google Maps contract.

### Games

- [Amazon GameLift Servers](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-gamelift-servers.html): Runs and scales the game servers for a multiplayer game.
- [Amazon GameLift Streams](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-gamelift-streams.html): Runs a game on an AWS machine and streams the video to a player's browser or device.
- [Open 3D Engine](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/open-3d-engine.html): A free 3D game and simulation engine you download and build with.

### General

- [AWS Marketplace Dark](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-marketplace-dark.html): Not a service. It is the dark background version of the AWS Marketplace icon.
- [AWS Marketplace Light](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-marketplace-light.html): Not a product. It is the light-background version of the AWS Marketplace icon.

### Internet of Things

- [AWS IoT Core](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-core.html): It is the front door where your gadgets connect to AWS and send messages.
- [AWS IoT Device Defender](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-device-defender.html): It watches your connected devices for signs that one has been tampered with.
- [AWS IoT Device Management](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-device-management.html): It helps you keep track of and update a large number of devices at once.
- [AWS IoT Events](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-events.html): A service, now being retired, that watched device readings and reacted when a pattern appeared.
- [AWS IoT ExpressLink](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-expresslink.html): A ready made connectivity chip, so a simple product can reach AWS without you writing network code.
- [AWS IoT FleetWise](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-fleetwise.html): It collects data from vehicles, choosing what to send so you do not pay for every signal.
- [AWS IoT Greengrass](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-greengrass.html): It runs AWS style code on your own hardware, near the machines, even without internet.
- [AWS IoT SiteWise](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-sitewise.html): It collects readings from factory machines and stores them in a way that matches how the plant is laid out.
- [AWS IoT TwinMaker](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iot-twinmaker.html): Builds a live 3D model of a real factory or building that updates from its sensors.
- [FreeRTOS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/freertos.html): A tiny free operating system that runs on very small chips inside devices.

### Management and Governance

- [AWS AppConfig](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-appconfig.html): Changes a setting in your running app without redeploying the code.
- [AWS Application Auto Scaling](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-application-auto-scaling.html): Adds and removes capacity automatically for AWS services other than plain servers.
- [AWS Auto Scaling](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-auto-scaling.html): One screen to set up scaling across several services at once.
- [AWS Backint Agent](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-backint-agent.html): Backs up an SAP HANA database straight into S3 using SAP's own backup screens.
- [AWS Chatbot](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-chatbot.html): Sends AWS alerts into Slack or Microsoft Teams, and lets you run some commands from the chat.
- [AWS CloudFormation](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloudformation.html): Writes your whole setup as a file, so you can rebuild it exactly.
- [AWS CloudTrail](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloudtrail.html): Records who did what in your AWS account.
- [AWS Config](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-config.html): Records how your AWS setup changes over time.
- [AWS Console Mobile Application](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-console-mobile-application.html): The official AWS app for your phone, for checking things while away from a laptop.
- [AWS Control Tower](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-control-tower.html): Sets up a tidy, rule enforced group of AWS accounts for a company.
- [AWS DevOps Agent](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-devops-agent.html): An AI assistant that digs into why your system broke and suggests the fix.
- [AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-distro-for-opentelemetry.html): AWS's own build of the standard open source tool that collects traces and metrics from your app.
- [AWS Health Dashboard](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-health-dashboard.html): Tells you when AWS itself has a problem, including ones that affect only your account.
- [AWS Launch Wizard](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-launch-wizard.html): A guided form that builds the AWS setup for a few specific packaged applications.
- [AWS License Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-license-manager.html): Keeps count of software licences you own so you do not go over what you paid for.
- [AWS Management Console](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-management-console.html): The AWS website where you click around to see and change your stuff.
- [AWS Organizations](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-organizations.html): Manages many AWS accounts as one company.
- [AWS Partner Central](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-partner-central.html): The website AWS resellers and software vendors use to manage their AWS partnership.
- [AWS Proton](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-proton.html): A way for a platform team to publish ready made deployment templates for developers, now being shut down.
- [AWS Resilience Hub](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-resilience-hub.html): Scores how well your app would survive a failure, and tells you what is missing.
- [AWS Resource Explorer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-resource-explorer.html): Search across all your AWS resources in every region at once.
- [AWS Service Catalog](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-service-catalog.html): An internal menu of approved setups that staff can deploy without free rein.
- [AWS Service Management Connector](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-service-management-connector.html): Retiring. It let ServiceNow or Jira users request and see AWS resources from their own ticket tool.
- [AWS Sustainability](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-sustainability.html): Not a service. It is AWS's environment programme, with one real tool for your carbon numbers.
- [AWS Systems Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-systems-manager.html): Manage all your servers from one place.
- [AWS Telco Network Builder](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-telco-network-builder.html): Deploys and manages mobile network software for phone companies running 5G on AWS.
- [AWS Trusted Advisor](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-trusted-advisor.html): Checks your account and suggests fixes.
- [AWS User Notifications](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-user-notifications.html): One place to decide which AWS events reach you, and where they land.
- [AWS Well Architected Tool](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-well-architected-tool.html): A questionnaire about your system that produces a list of the risks you have not handled.
- [Amazon CloudWatch](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-cloudwatch.html): Watches your systems and tells you when something is wrong.
- [Amazon Managed Grafana](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-managed-grafana.html): Runs Grafana dashboards for you so nobody has to patch a Grafana server.
- [Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-managed-service-for-prometheus.html): Stores and queries Prometheus metrics for you, without running Prometheus servers.

### Media

- [AWS Deadline Cloud](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-deadline-cloud.html): It runs your 3D renders and other heavy creative jobs on rented computers.
- [AWS Elemental Appliances & Software](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-appliances-software.html): It is the name for the video encoding boxes and software AWS sells you to run in your own building.
- [AWS Elemental Conductor](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-conductor.html): It is the control panel that manages a room full of Elemental encoders.
- [AWS Elemental Delta](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-delta.html): It stores and hands out live video in your own building so thousands of viewers can watch it.
- [AWS Elemental Link](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-link.html): A small box you plug a camera into, and the video goes straight to AWS.
- [AWS Elemental Live](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-live.html): Software or a box in your building that turns a live camera feed into internet streams.
- [AWS Elemental MediaConnect](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-mediaconnect.html): It moves a live video feed from one place to another without losing quality.
- [AWS Elemental MediaConvert](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-mediaconvert.html): It converts video files you already have into the formats players can stream.
- [AWS Elemental MediaLive](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-medialive.html): It takes a live camera or stream and turns it into something viewers can watch.
- [AWS Elemental MediaPackage](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-mediapackage.html): It hands your live video to viewers in whatever format their player wants, and can record it.
- [AWS Elemental MediaStore](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-mediastore.html): It was fast storage made for live video, and AWS has now shut it down.
- [AWS Elemental MediaTailor](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-mediatailor.html): It slips adverts into a video stream so they play like part of the programme.
- [AWS Elemental Server](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elemental-server.html): Software in your own building that converts recorded video files into streaming formats.
- [AWS Thinkbox Deadline](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-thinkbox-deadline.html): Free software you install yourself to manage a render farm.
- [AWS Thinkbox Frost](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-thinkbox-frost.html): A 3ds Max plugin that turns clouds of particles into a solid surface you can render.
- [AWS Thinkbox Krakatoa](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-thinkbox-krakatoa.html): Free desktop software that renders huge clouds of particles, like smoke, dust and fire.
- [AWS Thinkbox Stoke](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-thinkbox-stoke.html): Free 3ds Max plugin that simulates particles moving through fields of motion.
- [AWS Thinkbox XMesh](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-thinkbox-xmesh.html): Saves moving 3D animation to disk so an artist can replay it fast.
- [Amazon Interactive Video Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-interactive-video-service.html): It gives you live streaming with chat, like a Twitch style channel, with very little setup.

### Migration and Transfer

- [AWS Application Discovery Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-application-discovery-service.html): It surveys the servers in your data centre so you know what you actually have before moving.
- [AWS Application Migration Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-application-migration-service.html): It copies your existing servers, as they are, onto EC2 and lets you cut over.
- [AWS Data Transfer Terminal](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-data-transfer-terminal.html): Lets you drive your hard drives to an AWS building and copy them in over a very fast cable.
- [AWS DataSync](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-datasync.html): It copies large amounts of files from one place to another, and checks they arrived.
- [AWS Mainframe Modernization](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-mainframe-modernization.html): Tools to move old mainframe programs to AWS, either running them as they are or rewriting them into Java.
- [AWS Migration Evaluator](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-migration-evaluator.html): Looks at the servers you own today and estimates what they would cost on AWS.
- [AWS Transfer Family](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-transfer-family.html): An SFTP server that saves files straight into S3.
- [AWS Transform](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-transform.html): An AI agent that reads your old applications and rewrites them for AWS.

### Networking and Content Delivery

- [AWS App Mesh](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-app-mesh.html): A retired traffic controller that used to sit next to each of your services.
- [AWS Client VPN](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-client-vpn.html): Lets staff on laptops anywhere dial into your private AWS network.
- [AWS Cloud Map](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloud-map.html): A phone book your services look things up in instead of hard coding addresses.
- [AWS Cloud WAN](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloud-wan.html): One place to build and see your whole global network instead of wiring regions together by hand.
- [AWS Direct Connect](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-direct-connect.html): A private cable from your building or data centre into AWS, instead of going over the internet.
- [AWS Global Accelerator](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-global-accelerator.html): Gets users onto the AWS network early so their traffic takes a faster path to your servers.
- [AWS Interconnect](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-interconnect.html): Orders a private cable between AWS and another cloud or your office, in a few clicks.
- [AWS PrivateLink](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-privatelink.html): Lets your private network reach an AWS service or a partner's service without touching the internet.
- [AWS RTB Fabric](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-rtb-fabric.html): Carries advertising bid requests between ad companies in a few milliseconds.
- [AWS Site to Site VPN](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-site-to-site-vpn.html): An encrypted tunnel over the internet joining your office network to your AWS network.
- [AWS Transit Gateway](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-transit-gateway.html): A central hub that connects all your networks so you stop wiring each pair together.
- [AWS Verified Access](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-verified-access.html): Staff reach internal apps over the internet without a VPN, and every request is checked.
- [Amazon API Gateway](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-api-gateway.html): The front door for your API.
- [Amazon Application Recovery Controller](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-application-recovery-controller.html): Big red switches that move your traffic away from a broken region or zone, and checks that the backup is really ready.
- [Amazon CloudFront](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-cloudfront.html): Keeps copies of your files near your users so pages load fast.
- [Amazon Route 53](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-route-53.html): The phone book that turns your domain name into an address.
- [Amazon VPC Lattice](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-vpc-lattice.html): Connects your services to each other by name, with permissions and routing handled for you.
- [Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-virtual-private-cloud.html): Your own private section of the AWS network.
- [Elastic Load Balancing](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/elastic-load-balancing.html): Shares incoming traffic across several servers.

### Quantum

- [Amazon Braket](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-braket.html): Lets you send programs to real quantum computers, or to simulators of them, and get results back.

### Satellite

- [AWS Ground Station](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-ground-station.html): Rents you time on satellite dishes to talk to your satellite, by the minute.

### Security and Identity

- [AWS Artifact](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-artifact.html): A self-service download page for AWS's own audit and compliance reports.
- [AWS Audit Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-audit-manager.html): It collects evidence about your AWS setup automatically so an audit is less painful.
- [AWS Certificate Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-certificate-manager.html): Free HTTPS certificates that renew themselves.
- [AWS CloudHSM](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-cloudhsm.html): A dedicated tamper-proof box that holds your encryption keys, and only you can open it.
- [AWS Directory Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-directory-service.html): It runs Microsoft Active Directory for you, or connects AWS to the one you already have.
- [AWS Firewall Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-firewall-manager.html): It pushes the same firewall rules to every account in your company automatically.
- [AWS IAM Identity Center](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-iam-identity-center.html): One login that gets your staff into all your AWS accounts, with the right permissions.
- [AWS Identity and Access Management](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-identity-and-access-management.html): Decides who can do what in your AWS account.
- [AWS Key Management Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-key-management-service.html): Creates and guards the keys that encrypt your data.
- [AWS Network Firewall](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-network-firewall.html): A firewall that inspects traffic going in and out of your private network in AWS.
- [AWS Payment Cryptography](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-payment-cryptography.html): It does the card-industry encryption work that bank payment systems need.
- [AWS Private Certificate Authority](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-private-certificate-authority.html): It lets you issue your own certificates for things inside your own network.
- [AWS Resource Access Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-resource-access-manager.html): Lets one AWS account share a specific resource with another account.
- [AWS Secrets Manager](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-secrets-manager.html): A safe for passwords and API keys.
- [AWS Security Agent](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-security-agent.html): An AI helper that attacks and reviews your own application to find holes.
- [AWS Security Hub](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-security-hub.html): One screen that gathers security problems from all your AWS security tools.
- [AWS Security Incident Response](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-security-incident-response.html): AWS security experts help you handle a breach, and the service triages alerts in between.
- [AWS Shield](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-shield.html): Protection against attacks that try to flood your site.
- [AWS Signer](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-signer.html): It digitally signs your code so the thing running it can check nobody tampered with it.
- [AWS WAF](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-waf.html): A filter that blocks bad web traffic before it reaches you.
- [Amazon Cloud Directory](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-cloud-directory.html): Stores objects like people and devices in several overlapping trees at once.
- [Amazon Cognito](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-cognito.html): Sign up and log in for your app's users, ready made.
- [Amazon Detective](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-detective.html): After an alert, it shows you the story of what actually happened.
- [Amazon GuardDuty](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-guardduty.html): Watches for signs that someone has broken in.
- [Amazon Inspector](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-inspector.html): It keeps checking your servers, containers and functions for known security holes.
- [Amazon Macie](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-macie.html): It looks through your S3 buckets for personal data you did not know was there.
- [Amazon Security Lake](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-security-lake.html): It puts all your security logs in one place, in one standard format.
- [Amazon Verified Permissions](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-verified-permissions.html): Decides whether a user is allowed to do a thing in your app, so you do not code it yourself.

### Storage

- [AWS Backup](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-backup.html): One place to schedule backups of everything.
- [AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-elastic-disaster-recovery.html): It keeps a live copy of your servers in AWS so you can start them if the originals die.
- [AWS Snowball](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-snowball.html): AWS posts you a rugged box, you copy data onto it and post it back.
- [AWS Snowball Edge](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-snowball-edge.html): A rugged box AWS posts you, which you fill with data and post back.
- [AWS Storage Gateway](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/aws-storage-gateway.html): A small piece of software in your office that makes AWS storage look like a local drive.
- [Amazon EFS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-efs.html): A shared folder that many servers can read and write at the same time.
- [Amazon Elastic Block Store](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-elastic-block-store.html): The hard disk attached to your EC2 server.
- [Amazon FSx](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-fsx.html): The family name for AWS's managed versions of four real file systems.
- [Amazon FSx for Lustre](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-fsx-for-lustre.html): A file system built for hundreds of machines reading the same data very fast.
- [Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-fsx-for-netapp-ontap.html): Real NetApp storage, run by AWS, with the same tools your storage team already knows.
- [Amazon FSx for OpenZFS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-fsx-for-openzfs.html): A fast Linux file share with snapshots, run by AWS.
- [Amazon FSx for WFS](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-fsx-for-wfs.html): A Windows file share, the kind with drive letters, run by AWS.
- [Amazon File Cache](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-file-cache.html): A temporary fast copy of files that actually live somewhere slower.
- [Amazon S3 on Outposts](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-s3-on-outposts.html): Gives you S3 buckets on AWS hardware sitting in your own building.
- [Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-simple-storage-service.html): A place to keep files, as many as you want.
- [Amazon Simple Storage Service Glacier](https://aws.4bittechnology.com/s/amazon-simple-storage-service-glacier.html): Very cheap storage for files you almost never open.
